text.p: Gainsco Inc chief executive Joseph Macchia said he believes the company can meet its 1996 earnings target of $0.90 a share.
"We believe there's room for cautious optimism," he told Reuters in an interview.
Wall Street has a 1996 consensus estimate of $0.87 a share, according to First Call.
Gainsco reported third quarter earnings of $0.15 a share, slightly below Wall Street's consensus. For the first nine months of 1996, Gainsco reported earnings of $0.55 a share.
Macchia said he believes the company can reach the high end of its 1996 gross premium goal of $110 million to $120 million.
The company would need gross premiums of $120 million and a loss ratio, including incurred, but not reported (IBNR) losses, of 42 percent to meet its earnings goal, he said.
Macchia believed those goals were within reach because of "huge commitments" its received from its agents.
Volume commitments to one of its key competitors have been mostly met for the year, giving the agents the opportunity to give more of their business to Gainsco, he said.
In addition, Macchia said, Gainsco was "calling in markers" with its agents, reminding "them of what we've done for them" so it can make its targets.
"The agents all have the business, it's who they're giving it to," Macchia said.
Macchia attributed the third quarter earnings shortfall to unfavorable court rulings in disputed claims.
Excluding those unfavorable judgments, he said, Gainsco would have made Wall Street's third quarter earnings targets.
He expects intense competition in the Texas excess and surplus lines market to continue in the near term. But in the long term, he expects to see the competition fade.
